walkthrough_label: Patient S1-E - the planned patient with an inflamed gallbladder
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out, but the pain is bad today.

presentation.summary: Mrs Rabia, 48, booked for planned gallbladder removal, arrives with constant pain for 2 days and felt hot overnight: she now has an acute illness.

history.answer: Constant pain under the right ribs for two days; I felt hot and shivery overnight.
No yellow eyes. Urine normal colour.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.
Dry toast yesterday at noon; nothing since because of the pain.
Last period 3 weeks ago; she agrees to a test.

observations.note: NEWS2 2 as the book states: HR 108 (1) + T 38.4 (1).

examination.finding: Tender under the right ribs; Murphy's sign positive.
Tender under the right ribs; no guarding elsewhere; no palpable lump.

scores.name: NEWS2
scores.note: HR 108 (1) + T 38.4 (1) as the book states; recomputed

scores.name: Tokyo 2018 grade
scores.note: WBC 15.2 not above 18; symptoms under 72 hours; no mass; no organ failure

problems.label: Acute cholecystitis (inflamed gallbladder), definite by Tokyo 2018
problems.why: A planned patient with local signs (Murphy's), systemic inflammation (WBC, CRP, fever) and a scan with a thick wall and fluid is no longer a routine list patient.
expected_actions: Recognise A (local signs), B (systemic signs) and C (imaging)
Do not take her on today's planned list as a routine case
Senior surgeon review; antibiotics per protocol; move to the acute pathway

decisions.prompt: Mrs Rabia has fever, a positive Murphy's sign, WBC 15.2, CRP 96 and a scan with a 6 mm wall and fluid. What now?

options.text: She has acute cholecystitis (Grade I): not suitable for the routine list; senior review, antibiotics and the acute pathway
options.consequence: Matches the book; early keyhole surgery is usually the plan.

options.text: Proceed with the planned operation as booked
options.consequence: She is acutely ill; the elective pathway no longer applies.
Fever and raised inflammatory markers need review today.

correct: Notice fever and tachycardia in a planned patient

incorrect.shows: The anaesthetist finds T 38.4 at Sign In
incorrect.risk: An acutely infected patient anaesthetised as elective

missed: Does not take a temperature: the inflammation is missed until the anaesthetist checks
recovery: Repeat vital signs, send bloods, call the senior

recognised: Tokyo A, B and C combined
debrief.priority: Acute cholecystitis in a planned patient
debrief.why_priority: The pathway changes from elective to acute
debrief.related: Local signs, systemic signs and the scan fit together
debrief.if_ignored: Worsening infection and a delayed operation
debrief.remember: Planned patients can arrive unwell: always take the temperature

responsible_adult.text: My sister is coming for me and she will stay with me tonight.

asa.why: A planned patient now unwell with an inflamed gallbladder, no organ failure: mild systemic illness (ASA 2) to severe (ASA 3).
